title: Lunchbox — feedback brief & probe recipes (Jun 2029)
content:
One‑page lunchbox for rapid field handoff — compact synthesis of recent customer threads, a small set of low-effort probes we can run in the next 10 workdays, and a short risk map for engineering. Meant to be shared with Eng PM + Solutions for quick prioritization calls.

Executive snapshot:
- Core signal: multiple mid‑market customers report intermittent latency spikes (50–200ms additional p50) when model context contains large chat histories + system-level metadata. Often correlates with prefix cache misses and route fallbacks.
- Secondary signal: customers want a simple control in the API/Console to prefer cost‑efficient variants (quantized or smaller model) under defined SLAs — currently too manual.
- Impact: 3 named customers (ApexRetail, LinguaPro, Xmerce) have flagged this as blocker to rollout; estimated potential ARR risk if unresolved = medium.

Representative quotes (verbatim from CS threads):
- "We see token bursts at night. Not sure if it's retry jitter or model swap — app becomes unusable for some reps." — LinguaPro customer support
- "Can we lock to a cheaper model when latency > X? We don't want to swap to a new API path." — product manager at ApexRetail

Top themes (clustered):
- Latency & fallback behavior (prefix: cache misses, model routing)
- Operational controls for cost-vs-latency tradeoffs (console toggles, API flags)
- Better telemetry surfaced for long chat sessions (per-chat KV cache hit rate, fallback counts)
- Small feature asks: per-route preferred-model list; per-tenant batching hints; clearer billing signaling when quantization applied

Quick wins (<= 2w dev + roll):
1) Probe: "kv-hit dashboard card" — add a per-route card in Console showing KV cache hit rate for last 24h and top 5 chats with lowest hit rates. Goal: make cache misses visible so CS can correlate with incidents.
   - Owner: Priya Desai (CS) / Console eng contact: Marcus Liu
   - Success metric: reduce time-to-triage from report -> root cause by 60% in trial customers
   - Linked ticket: JIRA-CS-871

2) Probe: "prefer-variant" API flag (beta) — a simple header/param that prefers cheaper model variants but allows automatic fallback only if latency SLO would be violated. Implement server-side policy to attempt preferred variant first.
   - Owner: Ethan Kim (Solutions) / Eng PM: TBD
   - Rollout path: 1) internal dogfood, 2) opt-in for three customers, 3) broader beta
   - Risk: subtle quality regressions; need eval harness and guardrails

3) Probe: lightweight retry-telemetry patch — instrument requests that trigger model fallback with a short breadcrumb in logs (reason, context-length, prefix-cache-hit=false). Expose aggregated counts in Console.
   - Low risk, high info value.

Medium bets (>= 4w):
- Auto-tiering policy: automated routing that selects cheapest compatible variant respecting latency SLOs per tenant — requires routing policy engine changes + offline eval dataset.
- Compact prompt inspector: sample and anonymize long conversations to show tokens that cause cache churn; privacy review required.

Risk map & unknowns:
- Privacy: sampling chat histories for the prompt inspector will need legal signoff and opt-in controls.
- Quality regression: prefer-variant flag may degrade outputs for some user prompts; need A/B test and fallback thresholds.
- Observability surface: current traces group requests in a way that loses per-chat context; adding low-level breadcrumbs may increase storage and cost.

Data notes (what we saw):
- ApexRetail: repeated incidents at 02:00–04:00 PST, median context length 3.2k tokens, KV-cache hit rate ~12% for affected chats.
- LinguaPro: saw fallbacks to smaller model when GPU pool autoscaler triggered surge policy.
- Xmerce: wants a console toggle to cap monetary spend per-route per-day.

Suggested experiments (concrete):
- Experiment A: enable kv-cache visibility for ApexRetail and LinguaPro for 2 weeks. CS to collect incident timestamps and correlate. Hypothesis: visibility alone reduces incident escalations.
- Experiment B: roll prefer-variant flag for 50k requests/day across two internal routes with QA checks. Monitor perplexity delta / user complaint rate.
- Experiment C: deploy retry-telemetry patch to staging and run a 7‑day synthetic workload to capture fallback frequency.

Operational/implementation hints for Eng: (notes to make the probes cheap)
- KV-card: reuse existing aggregated metrics pipeline; front-end only needs a new card and a small query for lowest hit chats.
- prefer-variant: implement as a routing hint that attempts a single trial request to preferred variant with a short deadline; if deadline exceeded, fallback to existing policy. Keep it opt-in to avoid global chaos.
- telemetry breadcrumbs: piggyback on existing trace IDs, add a small boolean tag for fallback_reason.

Open questions for leadership / next sync:
- Do we want a product-level knob (Console) or keep this API-only? Quick wins favor Console card first.
- Tolerance for output-quality regressions vs cost savings — propose a 2% quality budget for initial experiments.

Next steps (10-day cadence):
- Day 0–2: Priya to enable kv-card queries for ApexRetail + LinguaPro; Marcus to scope front-end card (est. 2d).
- Day 3–6: Engineering spike to prototype prefer-variant header (small POC).
- Day 7–10: Run Experiment A + C, collect results, prepare short findings doc.

Owners & viewers:
- Primary: Sasha Moreno (CS), Marcus Liu (Console), Priya Desai (CS ops), Ethan Kim (Solutions eng)
- Keep Eng PMs looped: @eng-components

Notes to self / trailing thoughts:
- Keep language of any customer-facing doc explicit about opt-in and quality guardrails.
- Consider low-friction billing cap (route-level soft cap) as a separate small-feature play — often requested and likely low-risk.
- Save a short slide deck for Sales to explain "prefer-variant" behavior vs SLA guarantees.

Attachments / raw threads: see linked artifacts above.

-- end of lunchbox brief --

Unresolved snippets to capture later:
- Exact cost delta when using 8-bit quantized variant under current billing — finance to calculate (ACTION: Marcus)
- Legal checklist for sampled prompt inspector (ACTION: Sasha to loop security/compliance)
